verified.notes: Packed tarball 0.2.0 installed into an owned, disposable, non-Desktop web profile created from the shipped template (DSH 0.2.2-rc.1). dsh --profile <test> --dump-config composed the bundle row; a bounded real startup served the Web app; the authenticated browser transport exercised the exact /api/skillre-sticky-wall/execute route: list, create, update, move (placement echoed back without bumping updatedAt), an out-of-bounds move CLAMPED into the world while a non-finite one is refused as sticky-wall/bad-request, arrange, archive, delete, plus storage persistence of both the note and its canvas placement across a full restart, and an unauthenticated request returning 401. Cleanup stopped every owned process, removed the owned profile root and verified it was gone. The real DSH Web UI was then driven in headless Chromium against a FRESH owned profile: the 便签墙 sidebar entry appeared and selected the panel (the shell's own preview-notice mask was dismissed first, otherwise it swallows pointer input), the wall mounted with the seeded welcome note, the composer created a note whose Markdown body rendered as strong/code/list elements with no literal markers left, pin moved it first, search filtered to it, archive hid it from the default wall, the archived toggle showed it again, the note survived a full page reload, canvas cards were absolutely positioned from stored layouts, a real pointer drag wrote a new placement through the Host, 整理 repacked the wall and left NO overlapping cards, grid and list views rendered the same note set, and the note palette switched between light and dark. 24/24 UI assertions passed with no uncaught errors. Cleanup stopped the harness, killed Chrome, removed both the owned profile and the Chrome scratch directory, and verified they were gone. The display contract was verified offline: meta.detail resolves to docs/DETAIL*.md, each carries exactly one banner image at the 640x300 ratio, and both SVGs render (evidence PNGs committed). Two real defects were found and fixed during this verification: card heights were under-estimated for CJK text (so the tidy pass overlapped cards), and arrange packed only the live set (so an archived visible card stayed on top of tidied ones). A post-review pass fixed four defects the independent review found and proved each with a test that fails when the fix is reverted: (1) the height estimate charged a long title a flat 1.4 lines, so a 120-char CJK title estimated 104px against a rendered ~244px and tidy overlapped; the title and tag pills are now measured by columns. (2) The packer silently clamped cards past the world coordinate limit, pinning hundreds to one edge; the shelf width now scales with the wall and a 300-card worst case is asserted overlap-free. (3) Every drag wrote rotate: 0, destroying the tilt tidy applied; the drag now carries rotation through and the UI harness asserts it. (4) Derived preview positions were indexed off the filtered list, so legacy notes jumped while typing in the search box; the index now comes from the unfiltered snapshot. Rotation is also budgeted into the shelf gap, and the transport clamps instead of rejecting an out-of-bounds drag. 0.2.1 makes the drag direct: the canvas card no longer transitions its transform (which turned every per-frame write into an animation target and made the card trail the pointer), the drag flag moved from React state to a node attribute so pressing no longer re-renders the wall, pointer moves are coalesced into one write per animation frame, the pointer loop is registered once instead of per press, and the hover lift no longer overwrites the drag transform on the canvas. The UI harness caught a regression in that rewrite (the drop cleared the inline transform and stripped the card's tilt) and the fix is covered by a test. 0.3.0 gives the wall a centre and makes the canvas direct. Tidy now packs a phyllotaxis spiral centred on the world origin with a real spatial-grid collision check (no shelf estimate), and the finished disc is re-centred on its centre of mass; the camera opens on that middle and frames the whole wall, capped at 100%. The canvas became a clipping viewport with one transform-driven world instead of a padded scroll container, so panning and zooming cost zero React renders and dragging a card can no longer move the wall under it. Pan is drag-on-paper or wheel, zoom is ctrl/cmd+wheel anchored on the pointer, and reset re-frames the wall. The drop is optimistic: the card lands on its final world position before the Host round-trip. Cards are memoized and note objects are reconciled by identity, the per-note full-size wrapper element is gone, and body clamping follows the width preset. Verified in the real DSH Web UI with 31/31 assertions on a fresh owned profile, including a 14-note wall that tidies into a centred disc with zero overlaps (aspect ratio 0.94) and is framed at 54% by the camera, a real pointer drag that persists its placement and keeps its rotation, a real drag on empty paper that pans the camera by exactly the pointer delta, a wheel zoom that keeps the world point under the cursor fixed to under 2px, and a reset that re-frames the whole wall. The harness itself caught two real defects during this verification: the wheel listener was bound to a canvas node that did not exist yet while the wall was loading (so zoom silently did nothing), and a pan that ended inside a single animation frame was dropped entirely. Both are fixed and asserted. 0.4.0 turns the wall into a centre-anchored board. The tidy pass now packs a phyllotaxis RING that leaves a clear disc (CENTRE_RADIUS, measured to each card's nearest EDGE, not its centre) at the middle, and the re-centring shift is applied only when it preserves that reserve. The wall's middle is now its centrepiece: a time-aware greeting, a running tally and an always-available quick-capture field, rendered as a screen-space overlay that stays put under pan and zoom. The header and toolbar rows are gone — the canvas fills the whole window and every control lives in one floating dock along the bottom. Auto-framing measures the RENDERED card boxes from the DOM instead of deriving them, is capped at 100% and floored at 50% for legibility, and runs one animation frame after the reconcile so tidy frames the wall it actually produced. Canvas cards are rendered at exactly the height the Host estimated, which is what makes the packer's collision geometry true by construction. Verified in the real DSH Web UI with 36/36 assertions: the centrepiece sits at the exact viewport middle and does not move while panning, tidy leaves the centre clear with zero card overlaps, a 14-note wall tidies to a centred ring (offset 1,1; aspect 1.01), quick capture creates a note and clears the field, the canvas covers 100% of the page with a single-row dock, and a real drag, a paper pan and a pointer-anchored wheel zoom all behave. The harness caught four real defects during this pass: the wheel listener bound to a canvas that did not exist yet, a same-frame pan being dropped, tidy consuming a fit request against the pre-tidy bounds, and a fit floor that shrank a large wall to unreadable size.

evidence.artifact-envelope: tests/client-bundle.spec.ts loads lib/client.js through window.__ModuleLoader__.load and asserts one registration, only the seeded react modules, the Cordis client contract and both slot registrations
evidence.host-contracts: tests/transport.spec.ts drives the exact Fetch route with real Request objects; tests/store.spec.ts covers the domain-backed store; tests/plugin.spec.ts covers config resolution and Fiber-scoped lifetime
evidence.packed-payload-bytes: scripts/verify-isolated.mjs checks every required packed file exists in the installed package under the owned profile root

observations.pendingDetail: Verified in the standalone DSH Web application. The Desktop Client (Electron) was not exercised: its profile is managed by the application and cannot be driven by this CLI-based harness. A Desktop-targeted release must repeat the visual check there.
